The production of rcVSVs is based on the pVSV eGFP dG plasmid (available from Addgene), which contains the complete VSV genome with a deletion of the vsv-g gene and a convenient multiple cloning site between the matrix (M) and polymerase (L) genes that includes the MluI and NotI restriction sites. A heterologous env gene can be introduced by standard cloning procedures or by Gibson assembly. Primers for Gibson assembly typically contain 20–25 bp overlapping end sequences that match the plasmid sequences at the point of assembly. To generate rcVSVs, the resulting plasmid, which contains the VSV genome and heterologous env, is co-transfected with an additional 5 plasmids encoding for viral proteins and the T7 RNA polymerase (Lawson et al., 1995; Langlois et al. 2012). rcVSVs are rescued from the transfected cells and can be used for a variety of applications (Bresk et al., 2019; Case et al., 2020; Liberatore et al., 2019).17.Day 1: Design the primers for Gibson assembly (Table 1). steps.title: Detach and seed BHK‑21 cells
steps.instruction: Detach BHK‑21/WI‑2 cells with StemPro Accutase, count viable cells using trypan blue, add 5 × 10⁵ cells in 2 mL DMEM to each well of a 6‑well plate and incubate 24 h at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Prepare cells for transfection
steps.instruction: One hour before transfection, remove the existing medium and add 2 mL serum‑free, antibiotic‑free DMEM to each well (this ensures pH equilibration).

steps.title: Transfect cells with Env plasmid
steps.instruction: Transfect the cells with 0.4 µg of an Env‑expressing plasmid (e.g., pCAGGS‑2S‑del18 or pCDNA‑AD8‑M‑GCT) using Effectene according to the manufacturer’s protocol; alternatively, use calcium‑phosphate transfection prepared by mixing 2× HEPES Buffer (50 mM HEPES, 10 mM KCl, 12 mM Glucose, 280 mM NaCl, 1.5 mM Na₂HPO₄; pH 7.2), 2 M CaCl₂ and DNA as described in Ratnapriya et al. 2020. Incubate the transfected cells for two days without changing the medium (Effectene shows no significant cytotoxicity).

steps.title: Infect transfected cells with scVSV‑G
steps.instruction: At day 4, remove the medium, wash the cells three times with PBS, add 500 µL serum‑free DMEM, then add scVSV‑G (ΔG‑luciferase) at an MOI of 3. Incubate 1 h at 37 °C, gently shaking every 15 min.

steps.title: Neutralize residual VSV‑G and harvest scVSVs
steps.instruction: Wash the cells once with PBS, add 2 mL serum‑free DMEM containing a 1/1000 dilution of anti‑VSV‑G antibody (clone 8G5F11, catalog MABF2337‑100UG), and incubate 24 h at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂. Collect the supernatant, centrifuge at 500 × g, aliquot the virus and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Seed target cells for luciferase assay
steps.instruction: On day 5, seed 2 × 10⁴ target cells per well in a 96‑well white luminometer plate. Use cells that express the appropriate receptor (e.g., 293T‑ACE2 for SARS‑CoV‑2 spike or Cf2Th‑CD4/CCR5 for HIV‑1 AD8 Env).

steps.title: Dilute and infect target cells
steps.instruction: On day 6, prepare 10‑fold serial dilutions of the harvested scVSVs in DMEM ranging from 10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁸. Aspirate the medium from each well, add 100 µL of each dilution in triplicate, include a cell‑only control, and incubate 6 h at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Lyse cells and measure luciferase
steps.instruction: After infection, aspirate all medium, add 31 µL of firefly luciferase lysis buffer to each well, incubate 20 min at 20‑25 °C, and measure luminescence with a luminometer as described in Ratnapriya et al. 2020.

steps.title: Design Gibson assembly primers
steps.instruction: Design primers for Gibson assembly with 20‑25 bp overlaps matching the plasmid insertion site; aim for a melting temperature of ~60 °C using tools such as NEBuilder Assembly Tool or any DNA editor.

steps.title: Amplify env gene by high‑fidelity PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify the gene of interest (e.g., HIV‑1 AD8 env or SARS‑CoV‑2 spike) using a high‑fidelity polymerase (PfuUltra II Fusion, Agilent) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Gel‑purify PCR product
steps.instruction: Run the PCR amplicon on a 0.8 %–1.2 % agarose gel, excise the band of the correct size and extract DNA with the Wizard SV Gel and PCR Clean‑Up System (Promega). This step is optional for Gibson assembly but improves efficiency.

steps.title: Perform Gibson assembly and transform bacteria
steps.instruction: Set up the Gibson assembly reaction using NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix, incubate 15 min at 50 °C, transform the reaction into competent bacteria, plate on LB agar containing 50 µg/mL carbenicillin and incubate 16‑20 h at 30 °C.

steps.title: Culture colonies and isolate plasmid
steps.instruction: Pick 2‑3 well‑isolated colonies, inoculate each in 2 mL LB broth with 50 µg/mL ampicillin, grow 16‑20 h at 30 °C in a shaker, then perform a miniprep (e.g., Macherey‑Nagel). Verify insertion by restriction digest and sequence the env gene.
